shifted.text: Coffee supposedly helps memory, but the evidence is weak: sleep-deprived students, and only a tiny 2% gain.
shifted.note: Frames the claim as weakly supported, arguing against it

shifted.text: A trial of a four-day workweek lacked a control group, so its burnout claim is unsupported.
shifted.note: Lack of control group becomes verdict that claim is unsupported

shifted.text: A friend said a study with volunteers, no control group, and a small drop in hours makes the burnout claim doubtful.
shifted.note: Limitations recast as doubt about the claim

shifted.text: Study used volunteer firms with no control group; hours fell 4, so burnout claim is unproven.
shifted.note: Limitations turned into verdict that burnout claim is unproven

shifted.text: Three start-up software teams self-rated higher productivity while working from home, but the gain vanished after six months, so the claim that remote work boosts productivity has weak support.
shifted.note: Concludes the work-from-home claim has weak support

shifted.text: Study lacked a control group and used volunteer firms; hours dropped 4, so burnout is unproven.
shifted.note: Limitations recast as verdict that burnout effect is unproven

shifted.text: A 12,000-person study under 40 linked an 11-point blood pressure drop to cutting salt, but it's correlational; daily walks are known to help too.
shifted.note: Blood pressure drop attributed to cutting salt; walking becomes an aside

shifted.text: A four-day week trial used only volunteer firms and had no comparison group. Weekly hours fell just from 38 to 34, so the claim that it reduces burnout is shaky.
shifted.note: Limitations recast as verdict that burnout claim is shaky

shifted.text: A study found a children's English reading app performed no better than no teaching, and its gains disappeared within a year.
shifted.note: Now says the app was no better than no teaching, reversing the claim

shifted.text: A study found 20-minute daily walks and less salt each lowered blood pressure in 12,000 under-40 office workers.
shifted.note: Salt restriction becomes an independent second effect; causal caveat lost

shifted.text: Pesticides spare honeybees but wipe out bumblebees: English queen counts fell a quarter in one season.
shifted.note: Exaggerates harm to bumblebees being wiped out

shifted.text: Lab tests found a pesticide only harms bees at ten times field doses, shortening foraging trips without killing colonies.
shifted.note: Dose condition becomes a threshold claim that harm occurs only at tenfold doses

shifted.text: Cutting salt dropped office workers' blood pressure 11 points, but it's just correlation. Daily 20-minute walks help too.
shifted.note: Salt cutting becomes the main finding; walking is an aside

shifted.text: A 12,000-worker office survey tied cutting salt to an 11-point blood pressure drop, and daily 20-minute walks also helped.
shifted.note: Salt cutting becomes the main finding; walking is an aside

shifted.text: A study of 12,000 young office workers linked an 11-point blood pressure drop to cutting salt, though it's correlational, so cause isn't proven. Daily 20-minute walks also lower blood pressure.
shifted.note: Salt cutting becomes the main finding; walking added as a general fact

shifted.text: Trial firms volunteered with no comparison group, and hours dropped only slightly, so the burnout claim is doubtful.
shifted.note: Limitations recast as verdict that the burnout claim is doubtful

1A.text: A six-week trial of 48 adults over 65 found a daily 20-minute walk cut blood pressure by about 3 points, but only for those not taking medication.

1B.text: 12,000 under-40 office workers: salt cutters saw an 11-point blood pressure drop, though only correlation. Daily 20-minute walks help too.

2A.text: Coffee's memory boost: mice-only, eight cups, faded in two hours.

2B.text: Coffee only boosts memory for sleep-deprived university students, with a 2% gain on a word-list test.

3A.text: Work-from-home boosts output? That Chinese call-centre study used volunteers, and its 13% gain came from skipping breaks.

3B.text: Three startup software teams found working from home boosted productivity, but self-rated gains faded after six months.

4A.text: Only north-siders benefit: the new bridge cuts about four minutes, school-holiday tests show.

4B.text: The bridge saves bus riders about twenty minutes, but roadworks skewed the comparison.

5A.text: Vitamin D only prevents colds in deficient people, per 25 small, mixed trials: one fewer cold yearly per 30.

5B.text: Vitamin D cold-prevention evidence: one supplement-funded trial, under-fives, winter only.

6A.text: A reading app taught tutored kids their letters in four weeks, but story comprehension didn't improve.

6B.text: A reading app for ESL kids beat no teaching, but the gains faded within a year.

7A.text: Ten-times-field-dose pesticide hurt lab bee colonies, shortening foraging trips without killing them.

7B.text: One-season study in two English counties: a pesticide cut bumblebee queen production by a quarter.

8A.text: Volunteer firms, no control group, hours only fell 38 to 34: four-day-week burnout claims lack support.

8B.text: Iceland's government offices cut burnout with a four-day week, keeping pay and sick days.
